description: The urine barrel from Crew 15 weighed 400+ lbs and had to be offloaded onto the Twin Otter within the 2-hour arrival window.
response: The Engineer developed an ergonomic rolling method to manoeuvre the barrel into the trailer while upright. The barrel and 3 trailers of trash were loaded successfully.
lesson: Pre-plan the urine barrel offload as a named step in the arrival logistics brief. Assign an owner and rehearse the method. It is the heaviest single outbound item and cannot be left behind.
source_citation: SRC-hypatia-iii-brief, Part IV – Incident and emergency register, §4.3 Operational incidents, lines 650-655. Register Crew tag: 'C16'. Sol: occurred 'within the 2-hour arrival window'; sol 1 used for arrival day. Confidence (B) rationale: named-individual logistics narrative (the Engineer's rolling method); daily-report style, not a formal engineering log. Reclassification note (2026-08-26): originally classified Failure; on review, no equipment or process actually failed here — the entry's substance is the Engineer's newly-developed ergonomic rolling method for a known heavy-item handling challenge, explicitly recommended for future crews to rehearse. Reclassified to Process Innovation; outcome changed to Adopted to reflect that the method is intended to carry forward, not merely a one-off fix.
